headline: Hypotheses are testable predictions—educated guesses that can be proven right or wrong
universal_truth: Ideas that can't be tested can't be improved; make your beliefs falsifiable
fun_facts: A good hypothesis must be falsifiable—there must be a possible result that would prove it wrong
Einstein's relativity made specific predictions that could have disproven it—they didn't
Many business ideas fail because they were never tested as hypotheses before full commitment
discussion_questions: What assumptions are you making that you haven't tested?
How would you know if your current beliefs were wrong?
What experiments could test your important assumptions?

hook.script: A hypothesis is an educated guess you can test. 'This will work' is a hope. 'If I do X, Y will happen' is a hypothesis. The difference? Hypotheses can be proven wrong—and that's what makes them useful.

cliff.script: We often hold beliefs without testing them. Why is testability so valuable?

options.text: Testable ideas can be improved or discarded—if you can't test a belief, you can't know if it's wrong; untestable ideas can persist forever without improving or correcting
options.response: Yes. Testability enables learning. If there's no way to be wrong, there's no way to get righter. Making ideas testable is making them improvable.
Confirmation is part of it, but more importantly, testing allows falsification—proving ideas wrong...

fact1.title: Falsifiability
fact1.script: A good hypothesis can be proven wrong. That might seem like weakness, but it's strength. Ideas that can't be wrong can never be tested, corrected, or trusted.

fact2.title: Prediction Making
fact2.script: Good hypotheses make predictions: 'If X, then Y.' This creates tests. If Y happens, the hypothesis is supported. If not-Y happens, the hypothesis is challenged.

fact3.title: Life Hypotheses
fact3.script: You have hypotheses about life: 'If I work hard, I'll succeed.' 'If I'm kind, people will like me.' Are these tested? What evidence would prove them wrong?

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Ideas that can't be tested can't be improved. Make your beliefs falsifiable. Test your hypotheses.

outro.script: That's Day 295. Tomorrow, we'll explore asking nature questions—scientific inquiry. Until then, turn one of your assumptions into a testable hypothesis.

growTrack.title: Hypothesis Formation - What Can You Test?
growTrack.activity: Pick an assumption you're making about work, relationships, or life. Formulate it as a hypothesis: 'If I do X, Y will happen.' What evidence would support or refute it? How could you test it?
